news_summary: The 2027 EU budget prioritizes investment in research, connectivity, and civil protection, underscoring a commitment to innovation, infrastructure, and safety.

articles.title: Press release - 2027 EU budget: focus on research, connectivity and civil protection
articles.summary: On Wednesday, MEPs gave their final greenlight to the last annual budget of the 2021-2027 EU long-term budget framework.Committee on Budgets Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP
articles.content:
In a deal reached on Wednesday 11 November, Parliament and member state governments agreed to set the overall level of commitment appropriations (legal promises to pay in the same year or later) at €199.7 billion, and payment appropriations (actual payments made to beneficiaries) at €211.5 billion. In commitment appropriations, this sets the 2027 budget at 0.99% of the EU’s gross national income (GNI). Parliament secured an additional €300 million for its priorities compared to the Commission’s proposal, boosting investment in research, transport and energy networks, Erasmus+, civil protection, border management, military mobility, the EU’s neighbourhood, and humanitarian aid. The deal also includes stronger cybersecurity and security capabilities for the EU institutions and delegations.

Boosting Europe’s resilience, competitiveness and global role

Key increases compared with the Commission’s proposal include €39 million for the EU’s Southern and Eastern Neighbourhood, €30 million for humanitarian aid and €30 million for border management and migration. MEPs secured more research funding through Horizon Europe with €21.5 million extra, and for transport and energy networks an additional €22.5 million. For education, the Erasmus+ programme receives an additional €14 million and the civil protection mechanism is reinforced by €13.5 million. Further increases support military mobility (€10 million), and climate and environmental action (€10 million). See the full table for funding for programmes. More details are available in this background briefing .

Repayment costs for NextGenerationEU (NGEU) and the Ukraine Support Loan

The €4.9 billion NGEU over-run costs are to be dealt with as agreed previously through a “cascade mechanism”, designed to manage the borrowing costs and protect flagship programmes. The amount allocated to servicing the Ukraine Support Loan debt is set at €650 million, in line with the Commission’s proposal. The Parliament, Council and Commission have also acknowledged in a joint statement the possibility of covering the loan’s debt service costs by mobilising the Ukraine Support Loan special instrument in 2027.

The 2027 budget was adopted by 406 votes to 184, with 69 abstentions. Council endorsed the deal on Monday.

Quotes

“The EU budget is about more than figures: it reflects our priorities and the future we want. The 2027 budget is too focused on the past. Traditional policies matter, but today's realities – the war in Ukraine, geopolitical tensions, and technological rivalry – demand new priorities. We want the EU to do more on defence, security, innovation, and energy, but the current EU long-term budget leaves us with little room to respond to these challenges. As this is the last annual budget of the current framework, let this be a moment to reflect on how we use our resources,” said the chair of the Committee on Budgets, Johan Van Overtveldt (ECR, BE). (Watch the full plenary speech.)

“Next year’s budget will be the smallest in recent history. At 0.99% of the EU’s gross national income, it is even below the one per cent line demanded by the most frugal capitals. One may think that is enough to get by but it falls short of the ambition our union should aim for, especially if we want to remain one of the world's leading powers. We must not let 0.99% become a benchmark. That is why the proposed 0.97% for the next MFF is so worrying. Amid economic pressures, wars, and domestic politics across member states, reversing €1 billion in Council cuts and adding €300 million for EU programmes above the Commission's draft for 2027 is a realistic and respectable outcome,” said the general rapporteur for the EU’s 2027 budget (for section III - Commission), Nils Ušakovs (S&D, LV). (Watch the full plenary speech.)

“Our institutions must be able to fulfil their responsibilities today while preparing for tomorrow's challenges, such as a changing security environment, growing geopolitical uncertainty and rapid technological change. We must protect our buildings, our people, our communications, and sensitive information to safeguard our independence and continue serving citizens effectively. We have worked to ensure that our institutions' operational needs are properly addressed, with stronger security and the capacity to respond to challenges arising from digitalisation and AI. A well-functioning EU administration is one that delivers results for citizens,” rapporteur for the other sections, Michalis Hajipantela (EPP, CY) said. (Watch the full plenary speech.)

Background

More than 93% of the EU budget goes directly to EU programmes. The annual EU budget, which serves 27 countries and 450 million Europeans, is relatively small – on average €160-200 billion annually during the 2021 to 2027 period. This is comparable to the national budget of Poland, which serves 39 million people, and equivalent to 30% of the budget of Germany, which serves 84 million people. The EU budget delivers significant economic, social and political benefits despite representing approximately only 1% of the EU’s gross national income (GNI). (Source: Parliament and Commission)

articles.personality_title: EU approves 2027 budget to boost research, security, and climate action
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – The European Union (EU) plans its spending through a long-term budget covering several years. The 2021-2027 budget sets priorities for many areas, including research, transportation, and security. The 2027 budget is the last annual plan within this framework.

**What happened** – On November 11, 2026, the EU Parliament and member countries agreed on the 2027 budget. They set the total spending promises at about €199.7 billion and actual payments at €211.5 billion. This amount is just under 1% of the EU’s total income. Lawmakers added €300 million more than the original proposal to support key programs like research, transport, education (Erasmus+), civil protection, border control, military mobility, and climate actions.

**Impact** – This budget increase means more money for important projects that affect millions of Europeans. For example, research funding grew by €21.5 million, helping scientists develop new technologies. The Erasmus+ program, which allows students to study in different countries, received an extra €14 million. Civil protection and humanitarian aid also got more support, helping the EU respond better to emergencies and crises. The budget also strengthens cybersecurity and security in EU institutions, preparing for a safer future.

**What's next step** – The budget now moves to implementation, with funds going to the programs and projects approved. EU leaders and officials will monitor how the money is spent and plan for the next budget after 2027. They will also manage costs linked to borrowing and loans related to recovery from crises like the war in Ukraine.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The EU’s 2027 budget focuses on strengthening research, security, and climate efforts by increasing funding for programs that support Europe’s future challenges and opportunities.
articles.personality_title_fr: L’UE approuve le budget 2027 pour renforcer la recherche, la sécurité et l’action climatique
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – L’Union européenne (UE) planifie ses dépenses à travers un budget pluriannuel. Le cadre 2021-2027 fixe des priorités dans plusieurs domaines, comme la recherche, les transports et la sécurité. Le budget 2027 est le dernier plan annuel de cette période.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Le 11 novembre 2026, le Parlement européen et les pays membres ont trouvé un accord sur le budget 2027. Ils ont fixé les engagements à environ 199,7 milliards d’euros et les paiements à 211,5 milliards d’euros. Ce montant représente un peu moins de 1 % du revenu total de l’UE. Les députés ont ajouté 300 millions d’euros par rapport à la proposition initiale pour soutenir des programmes clés comme la recherche, les transports, l’éducation (Erasmus+), la protection civile, la gestion des frontières, la mobilité militaire et les actions climatiques.

**Impact** – Cette hausse de budget signifie plus de moyens pour des projets importants qui touchent des millions d’Européens. Par exemple, le financement de la recherche a augmenté de 21,5 millions d’euros, aidant les scientifiques à développer de nouvelles technologies. Le programme Erasmus+, qui permet aux étudiants d’étudier dans différents pays, a reçu 14 millions d’euros supplémentaires. La protection civile et l’aide humanitaire ont aussi été renforcées, améliorant la réponse aux urgences. Le budget renforce aussi la cybersécurité et la sécurité des institutions de l’UE, pour un avenir plus sûr.

**Prochaine étape** – Le budget va maintenant être appliqué, avec des fonds distribués aux programmes validés. Les dirigeants et responsables de l’UE suivront l’utilisation de l’argent et prépareront le prochain budget après 2027. Ils géreront aussi les coûts liés aux emprunts et prêts, notamment ceux liés à la guerre en Ukraine.

**En résumé** – Le budget 2027 de l’UE met l’accent sur la recherche, la sécurité et le climat en augmentant les financements pour des programmes qui préparent l’Europe aux défis et opportunités futurs.
articles.personality_title_es: La UE aprueba el presupuesto 2027 para impulsar la investigación, seguridad y acción climática
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La Unión Europea (UE) planifica sus gastos mediante un presupuesto a largo plazo que cubre varios años. El marco 2021-2027 establece prioridades en áreas como investigación, transporte y seguridad. El presupuesto de 2027 es el último plan anual dentro de este marco.

**Qué pasó** – El 11 de noviembre de 2026, el Parlamento Europeo y los países miembros acordaron el presupuesto para 2027. Fijaron los compromisos de gasto en unos 199,7 mil millones de euros y los pagos reales en 211,5 mil millones. Esta cantidad es menos del 1 % de los ingresos totales de la UE. Los legisladores añadieron 300 millones de euros más que la propuesta inicial para apoyar programas clave como investigación, transporte, educación (Erasmus+), protección civil, control fronterizo, movilidad militar y acciones climáticas.

**Impacto** – Este aumento de presupuesto significa más dinero para proyectos importantes que afectan a millones de europeos. Por ejemplo, la financiación para investigación creció en 21,5 millones de euros, ayudando a los científicos a desarrollar nuevas tecnologías. El programa Erasmus+, que permite a estudiantes estudiar en otros países, recibió 14 millones de euros extra. También se fortaleció la protección civil y la ayuda humanitaria, mejorando la respuesta a emergencias. El presupuesto también refuerza la ciberseguridad y la seguridad en las instituciones de la UE para un futuro más seguro.

**Próximo paso** – El presupuesto ahora se implementará, destinando fondos a los programas aprobados. Los líderes y funcionarios de la UE supervisarán el uso del dinero y planificarán el próximo presupuesto después de 2027. También gestionarán los costos relacionados con préstamos y deudas vinculadas a la recuperación de crisis como la guerra en Ucrania.

**Resumen en una frase** – El presupuesto 2027 de la UE se centra en fortalecer la investigación, la seguridad y el clima aumentando la financiación para programas que preparan a Europa para los desafíos y oportunidades futuras.
